newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power holds steady on nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power holds steady on nuke outage.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in New York held mostly steady Tuesday with support from uncertainty over the timing of a restart of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant, industry sources said.

The 910 megawatt (MW) Maine Yankee plant in Wiscasset, Maine had been expected to resume power production on Wednesday, but the company said Tuesday the station will be back on line "in the next few days."
"It (power price) is holding steady on the Maine Yankee uncertainty," one Northeast power trader said.

Also, New York Power Authority's 780 megawatt Fitzpatrick nuclear plant in Scriba, N.Y., was expected to synchronize to the electricity grid on Thursday following scheduled refueling and maintenance, the company said.
PECO Energy Co's 1,055 MW Limerick nuclear power unit 2 in Pottstown, Pa., could resume electricity production this weekend after tripping off line late Friday due to an oil leak, the company said.
Separately, about 60,000 New England utility customers were reported to be without power Tuesday morning after a storm dumped up to 18 inches of heavy, wet snow through the region over the weekend.
In the eastern portion of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday delivery was pegged at $29.00-34.00 from $28.00-32.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Monday.
Little business was said to be done in eastern NYPP, with marketers reluctant to pay the high prices offered by utilities, industry sources said.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Wednesday in eastern NYPP was notionally reported to be steady at $19.00-$20.00.
Western NYPP power for peak, non-firm delivery on Wednesday was quoted at $23.50-24.50 from $25.00-27.00 on Monday, the brokers and marketers said.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday at the Northeast Utilities border was reported steay to lower at $36.50-37.50 from $37.00-38.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Wednesday delivery to the NU border was assessed steady at $20.00-$21.00.
Temperatures through much of the Northeast were expected to reach maximums in the high 30s and mid-40s degrees Fahrenheit on Wednesday.
